I've been doing this for 15 years in Quzhou, and the wheat-maize rotation is what everyone around here does. My 5 mu isn't big, but with some family working in town, I'm not desperate — I can farm the way I know works.

**My thinking:**

For **wheat**, I'll plant in early October after maize harvest. I'll use a rotary tiller to work in the maize stubble — I've done it that way for years and the seedbed comes out fine. I use the Kenong 199 variety; most of my neighbors use it, the seed dealer carries it, and it handles our winters well. I'll apply the base fertilizer — compound fertilizer plus some extra urea — before sowing, then top-dress with urea at jointing in spring. I'll irrigate three times: once before sowing to ensure germination, the winter water before freeze, and jointing/heading. I'll spray herbicide in winter and do one fungicide pass around heading.

For **maize**, I'll plant right after wheat harvest in June — no time to waste. I don't bother plowing for summer maize, just direct seed into the stubble with rotary prep. Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335, whatever the dealer has — both are solid hybrids I trust. Fertilizer goes in two passes: base at planting, then urea side-dressed at big bell stage. Irrigation depends on rain, but I'll plan for two or three times. One herbicide spray right after emergence, one more pass if there's corn borer or aphids later.

I split my 5 mu evenly across both seasons since that's just how the rotation works — same land, same field, different time of year.
